subtitle: Discover how borrowing chords from parallel modes adds color and emotional depth

backLink.label: Back to Chord Theory in Songs

introduction.title: Borrowing From Parallel Worlds
introduction.text: Modal interchange is like having access to a parallel universe of your key. While staying in C major, you can borrow chords from C minor (or other C modes) to add emotional colors that pure major can't provide.

columns.title: Parallel Keys
columns.text: C major and C minor share the same tonic but have different scale tones, creating contrasting harmonic palettes.

columns.title: Emotional Colors
columns.text: Borrowed chords add darkness to major keys, brightness to minor keys, or modal flavors like blues or folk.

cards.title: The Power of bVI and bVII

fields.label: Analysis
fields.value: I - III - IV - iv (in G major)

items: Cm (iv): Borrowed from G minor
Creates immediate shift from bright to dark
The word "creep" lands on this borrowed chord

cards.title: Why It's Genius
items: Major progressions sound hopeful and confident
The borrowed iv chord introduces self-doubt
Perfect musical metaphor for the lyrics
The contrast is jarring but beautiful
Emotional Journey: Confidence → Brightness → Stability → Self-doubt

cards.title: Best Practices
items: Start with common borrowed chords (bVII, bVI, iv)
Use sparingly - too much loses the contrast
Consider the lyrics and emotional context
Practice voice leading between major and borrowed chords
Listen to how others use these chords

cards.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using too many borrowed chords - sounds unfocused
Ignoring voice leading - creates awkward jumps
Not considering the melody - some clash
Using borrowed chords just to be "sophisticated"
Forgetting the emotional purpose they serve

exercises.title: Beginner Practice
items: Practice I-bVII-IV in multiple keys
Replace IV with iv in simple progressions
Learn the parallel minor scale for any major key
Listen for borrowed chords in rock songs

exercises.title: Advanced Practice
items: Experiment with Dorian and Mixolydian borrowed chords
Reharmonize pop songs with modal interchange
Practice smooth voice leading with borrowed chords
Write progressions that tell emotional stories
